text:
maya: Quick heads-up — onboarding a community MistralX-like drop (config from repo) and hit a funky generation shift when running int4 conversion.
sam: Can you paste the minimal repro? config + command.
maya: repro is small. ran `python convert.py --model ./weights --quant int4 --rotary-mode auto` then `pytest tests/regression/test_infer.py::test_smoke`
deepak: Error symptoms?
maya: outputs are semantically similar but tokenized prefixes change after step ~6. sometimes repeats. logs show KV cache keys mismatch warnings.
alex: Hmm, KV cache mismatch usually points to token id offsets or rotary index mapping differences.
maya: Agreed. I dumped the first 24 token ids and the rotary cosine table shapes. cosine table looks transposed vs our expected layout.
sam: Did you check head dimension ordering? (heads x head_dim vs head_dim x heads)
zach: Also check whether the model uses per-head rotary scaling (freq per head) vs global — that flips reshape ops.
maya: Good call. I compared layer.0.attn.freq.shape: `(16, 64)` on the raw checkpoint, but our loader expects `(64, 16)`. when I swap axes locally, generation aligns.
deepak: That implies the exporter used a different head-major layout. We should add a compatibility shim in the converter with auto-detect.
ci-bot: Deploy queued: add-converter-shim-5060043210 by @sam
sam: I'll sketch a quick heuristic: if freq.shape == (n_heads, head_dim) vs (head_dim, n_heads) — and n_heads * head_dim == embed_dim — auto-transpose.
alex: Also validate tokenizer: we saw prefix shifts — could be tokenizer normalization (NFC vs NFKC) or sentinel token remap.
maya: Tokenizer check: raw vocab has both canonical and decomposed forms for some punctuation. Our tokenizer run used normalizer NFKC. The checkpoint seems trained on NFC.
deepak: If tokenizer normalizer differs we should try remapping via reversible normalization step before token ids.
sam: For int4 quant, did you use per-channel scale or global? per-channel cal tends to preserve logits ordering better.
maya: Used global by default. Re-ran with per-channel calibration and the hallucination/repeat reduced but not gone.
zach: Could be combined effect: rotary layout + tokenizer normalization + quant noise. Recommend isolate one change at a time.
maya: Plan: 1) create converter shim for rotary reshape auto-detect, 2) run tokenizer with NFC preprocessor and compare logits, 3) quantize with per-channel and run our eval suite.
alex: Add a short unit test: load raw checkpoint -> converted -> run sample prompt and assert top-5 token overlap >= 0.9 vs reference float32 conversion.
deepak: I'll add the test and a small flagged CI job `ml-compat-smoke`.
sam: I'll prototype the shim and push a wip PR. maya, can you attach the failing sample prompt & golden tokens to the PR?
maya: On it. attaching sample prompt + float32 golden outputs in PR comments.
ci-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/convert/pull/327 — WIP by sam
alex: Nicely scoped. If the shim resolves most issues we can add a converter mode `--adapter=auto-layout`.
maya: Thanks all — will run the three-step plan and report back with numbers (perplexity diffs + top-k overlaps).
sam: ping me when CI job is green, I'll fold into the docs and release notes.
ci-bot: CI job triggered: ml-compat-smoke (quick) #5060043227
zach: One more thought: if rotary uses fractional head scaling (headwise scale) we might need to apply sign-correction when transposing — watch for sign flips in small-angle cosines.
maya: noted. will include cosine sign-check dump in the debug artifacts.
